items.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Years ago when I was booking groups for school shows we had a group come from Albany, Alex Torres and the Latin Kings. ... [INTERVIEWEE] You’re not alone.

ctx.x: Yep. That’s a great, that’s a wonderful question. And only a musician, like you, would say that question. Yeah. Because I am a jazz musician and I’m hearing it come — I’m hearing what I hopefully want to do coming through having listened to Coltrane and Pharoah Sanders and Sam Rivers and McCoy Tyner. And just a long list of musical greats. And what you can do with simple melodic ideas, but beautiful harmonies, focusing on beautiful harmonies and then building on all the rhythmic beauty that Afro- Cuban music has…

Yeah. Years ago when I was booking groups for school shows we had a group come from Albany, Alex Torres and the Latin Kings. It was wonderful. And I got aggravated with myself because there was some times I couldn’t find one.
